tool.name: miaDash
tool.description: Interactive dashboard for the analysis and exploration of microbiome data

param.name: abundance_table
param.label: Abundance table (optional)
param.help: Tab-separated table with taxa in the rows: the first column holds the taxon ids and the header row holds the sample ids, e.g. OTU/S1/S2. It is imported as the assay of a TreeSummarizedExperiment. Leave this empty to upload from the browser or start from the example data that ships with the application.

param.name: coldata_table
param.label: Sample data / colData (optional)
param.help: Tab-separated table with samples in the rows: the first column holds the sample ids, which must match the header of the abundance table, and the remaining columns are sample variables (group, batch, ...). Leave this empty to start with an empty colData derived from the sample ids.

param.name: rowdata_table
param.label: Taxa data / rowData (optional)
param.help: Tab-separated table with taxa in the rows: the first column holds the taxon ids, which must match the row names of the abundance table, and the remaining columns are taxon variables (taxonomy ranks, ...). Leave this empty and tick 'Derive taxa from row names' if the row names of the abundance table are semicolon-separated taxonomy strings.

param.name: row_tree
param.label: Taxa tree (optional, Newick)
param.help: A phylogenetic tree in Newick format whose tip labels match the taxon ids of the abundance table. Needed for analyses that use the phylogeny (unifrac distances, philr transformation, tree-aware panels). Convert the dataset to plain text if this selector does not offer it.

param.name: taxa_from_rownames
param.label: Derive taxa from row names
param.help: Parse the row names of the abundance table as taxonomy strings (like k__Bacteria;p__Firmicutes;c__Bacilli) into taxonomy ranks, the same option as the 'Raw Data' tab inside the application.

tool.help:
`miaDash <https://github.com/microbiome/miaDash>`_ is the Microbiome Analysis Dashboard, an R Shiny application for building and exploring TreeSummarizedExperiment objects without writing code. It is built on `iSEE <https://isee.github.io/iSEE/>`_ and the `miaverse <https://microbiome.github.io/>`_ ecosystem: import data, manipulate it (subset, agglomerate, transform), compute quality and diversity summaries, and explore the result in interactive iSEE panels.
.. class:: infomark
**Input datasets.** All inputs are optional and the tool starts whether or not you provide them. The tables you select here are staged and pre-loaded into the application at launch, so the session starts from your data:
#. *Abundance table* - tab-separated, taxa in rows, first column the taxon ids, header row the sample ids. #. *Sample data (colData)* - tab-separated, samples in rows, first column the sample ids matching the abundance table header. #. *Taxa data (rowData)* - tab-separated, taxa in rows, first column the taxon ids matching the abundance table row names. #. *Taxa tree* - Newick, tip labels matching the taxon ids.
Anything you leave empty can still be added inside the application: the *Import* panel accepts uploads from the browser and its *Raw Data* tab takes the same table layouts, and the application ships with example datasets.
.. class:: infomark
**Results are sent to your Galaxy history.** The export download in the application has a *Send to Galaxy* button next to it. It saves the file in the *miaDash results* collection and starts a direct history upload in the background. The collection becomes available in the history when the interactive job ends, even if direct upload is unavailable, so anything you sent during the session is kept either way.
What this tool provides:
#. Import of raw tables or R objects into a TreeSummarizedExperiment #. Manipulation: subset by prevalence, agglomerate by rank, transform assays (including PhILR), all recorded as a reproducible R script #. Quality control, alpha/beta diversity, clustering and ordination #. Interactive exploration of all panels through iSEE, with export to TreeSE, phyloseq, BIOM, Mothur and QIIME2 formats
.. class:: infomark
**Citation**
Benedetti G, Seraidarian E, Pralas T, Jeba A, Borman T, Lahti L (2025). iSEEtree: interactive explorer for hierarchical data. *Bioinformatics Advances*. doi: https://doi.org/10.1093/bioadv/vbaf107
